CRSP: Ph1b sHTG data (n=10) showed day-30 TG -63% with no pancreatitis, durable at 90 days in 7 patients. A $3.9B cap on early human data, with $2.3B cash, and only 40% of Casgevy economics.
AUTL: AUCATZYL FY26 revenue guide is $140-150M and lupus has RMAT, but $248M cash against $360M debt and ~6.9 quarters of runway make funding the issue; Kyverna is further along in lupus CAR-T.
LYEL: Ronde-cel held 75% CR at 12 months in 3L+ LBCL (n=44), with ASH oral data on Dec 14 and pivotal data mid-2027. Cap of $485M vs $194M cash plus an $80M placement, in a crowded CD19 CAR-T field led by Breyanzi.
SNDX: Revuforj Q3 revenue of $60.7M (+90% y/y) sits against an $822M cap, and $551M cash roughly offsets $594M debt. Frontline AML data guided for Q4 2026 are the next driver.
IMMX: NEXICART-2 interim showed 40/45 complete responses in AL amyloidosis with no neurotoxicity, but it is a single-arm dataset and BLA timing has slipped to mid-2027. $341M cash covers about half the $645M cap.
ANTX: Epetraborole has no human efficacy data in polycythemia vera after a March repositioning; enrollment starts by YE26. A $206M cap is 2.6x cash of $80M, with rusfertide and divesiran already ahead.
PTGX: Icotrokinra (6-10% royalty) and rusfertide (14-29%) are both approved, $275M is due in Q4 and a $300M buyback is authorized. A $9.0B cap leaves value tied to J&J and Takeda launch execution.
XLO: A $152M cap sits against $122M cash, so little is priced into XTX501. First patient dosed Oct 2026, NSCLC data Q4 2027; IL-2 has a toxicity-failure history, so masking must prove out.
ELTX: Ph2 missed its ITT DFS primary and R0 subgroup (HR 0.65, p=0.048) is nominal; $24M cash vs a $37M cap means a Ph3 needs financing data may not support.
RXRX: TUPELO: 13/15 patients had polyp-burden reduction (median -47%) in rare orphan FAP, where no drug is approved. But a $1.7B cap against $562M cash is an AI-platform multiple on one small indication, so we see it as expensive until a second readout.
IBRX: Q3 revenue of $48.7M (+53% YoY) and a papillary label expansion are real. But the $6.6B cap carries $1.3B debt against $334M cash, with cretostimogene closing in.
TARA: Trades at its $143M cash value with Breakthrough status and 72% any-time CR (n=31, BCG-naive). Edge is BCG-sparing supply, not clearly better efficacy, in a crowded NMIBC field; 6.6 quarters of cash is tight.
JANX: Trades below its $946M cash at a $689M cap, so the PSMA x CD3 engager is priced as free: 30% PR (8/27), no Grade 3 CRS. Earlier PSMA BiTEs failed on CRS; next data 1H 2027.
OLMA: Cash of $414M covers 56% of the $744M cap into the binary OPERA-01 topline (Q1 2027, slipped from fall 2026). Elacestrant and camizestrant set the bar for this oral SERD.
ATOS: 26.5% breast-density cut matching tamoxifen is a biomarker, not an outcome, and financing may precede EVANGELINE data; a cash-backed show-me story, trading below $26M cash.
ZNTL: Cyclin E1+ ovarian cancer showed median OS of 15.9 vs 7.5 months in E1- patients, but the pivotal readout slipped to 1H 2027. Cap is below $229M cash, yet ~5 quarters of runway makes financing likely.
NXTC: Pending Avere merger leaves legacy holders ~2%, so real bet is a late oral IL-23 entrant w Ph2b data ~1H 2028, whatever screen shows from a $29M cap vs $400M cash.
CRBP: CRB-701 posted 42.9% cORR in 2L OPSCC and 34.4% in cervical (n=317 safety set), and cash of $115M exceeds the $70M cap. Astellas/Pfizer's EV is 2+ years ahead; 1L combo data come Q1 2027.
CGEM: Netting $314M cash, ~$300M of the $614M cap rides on CLN-978 (10/14 SLE pts with a 4+ point hSLEDAI drop; one Grade 3 CRS). December multi-dose data and the Feb 27 zipalertinib PDUFA are next.
WHWK: HWK-007 has no human efficacy data yet, and PTK7 ADCs have failed before (AbbVie's cofetuzumab pelidotin was discontinued). A $283M cap with $170M cash; first data due 1H 2027.
APLM: ORR of 64.5% (85.7% at GCN>=4) is competitive w capmatinib's ~68% and drug is China-approved, but $3M cash (CEO lent $2M) puts financing ahead of H1 2027 US IND.
IMCR: Kimmtrak sold $102.2M in Q3 ($324.8M YTD), and $901M cash vs $403M debt underpin a $1.5B cap. Upside rests on TEBE-AM OS (Q2 2027) and brenetafusp moving beyond uveal melanoma.
DRTS: The ReSTART single-arm pivotal (n=88) has not reported efficacy, yet the cap is $1.2B against $105M cash and about 7 quarters of runway. Expectations are high going into the topline.
ANL: AN9025 has no efficacy data after more than a year of dosing, ex-China rights only, and first data are due 1H27. A $646M cap is 2.8x its $232M cash, while Revolution Medicines already has randomized Ph3 results in the same space.
PBLS: Zolucatetide hit 72.2% ORR (13/18) at 32 weeks with no AE discontinuations, and FDA aligned on Ph3. But a $3.6B cap is 3.3x cash and PEDESTAL does not read out until 2029.
RCKT: A $241M cap is 0.9x cash, so the market ascribes little to Danon gene therapy RP-A501 despite FDA alignment on a pivotal Ph2 (success = 7 of 12). Topline is mid-2028, and the past clinical hold and AAV safety remain the overhang.
DMAC: ReMEDy2 has no topline; the Q1 2027 DSMB interim may only re-size the trial (300-728 pts), which would need more than $35M cash with ~4 quarters of runway. The $449M cap rests on an unread pivotal.
HUMA: Approved, but Q3 Symvess sales were only $1.0M. Three positive Ph3s and a dialysis sBLA targeted for Nov support the story; $65M cash against $37M debt and a 65% 12-month drop make dilution a real risk.
KRYS: VYJUVEK sales hit $127.3M in Q3 (+30%) and cash is $1.2B, but an $8.8B cap already prices in pipeline success. KB111 interim is due by YE2026; Abeona's ZEVASKYN is a durability threat in large wounds.
VRCA: VP-315 posted 97% ORR and 51% complete histologic clearance in BCC Ph2, and FDA agreed a two-trial Ph3 design. But $14M cash vs $12M debt on a $68M cap makes dilution the gate.
EYPT: LUGANO missed and LUCIA is do-or-die w AXPAXLI ahead, so at ~2.6 quarters of runway cash gets burned before it can be returned, even at 7x $31M cap after a 97% collapse.
SRZN: SZN-8141 has dosed its first DME patient with no efficacy data, and Ph1b reads only in 2H 2027. AXPAXLI, DURAVYU, 4D-150 and Zenkuda are far ahead, so a $616M cap on $100M cash looks stretched.
PTN: Going-concern doubt on $7.5M cash against a $10M cap, preclinical MC4R programs and Rhythm's IMCIVREE years ahead: dilution arrives before any Ph1 start.
IRWD: FDA wanted a second Ph3 (STARS-2, 2028) after STARS hit its primary, and Ironwood hired Goldman Sachs to explore strategic alternatives. $86M cash vs $325M debt; the $803M cap is up 83% in a year.
BCRX: ORLADEYO FY26 guidance is $625-645M, large against a $1.9B cap, and navenibart Ph3 reads out Q3 2027. $375M cash against $817M debt and injectable or CRISPR rivals temper the picture.
TRAX: ANB033 beat placebo in a small celiac Ph1b (VH:CrD +0.49, p=0.009), but FB102 shares the target with Ph2 data about a year ahead. A $2.0B cap vs $156M cash and 5.7 quarters of runway looks stretched.
ODTX: Open-label Ph2a showed 27% clinical remission at 20 mg BID (n=41) and 61% response with no SAEs, but no placebo arm. A $931M cap vs $387M cash; randomized Ph2b data are not due until 2H27, in a crowded UC field.
IPSC: An IND is a paper milestone: CNTY-813 has no human data until 2H 2027, while Vertex is already dosing and SANA files on a similar timeline. $338M cap, $174M cash.
VERA: Accelerated approval in Jul 2026, then strong final ORIGIN 3 data (HR 0.24); full-approval sBLA filed Nov 3 for mid-2027. A ~$1.9B cap vs $384M cash (3.8 quarters) faces Fabhalta, Filspari and Vertex's povetacicept.
CLYM: At 200 mg, 70% mean PLA2R reduction and 5/13 remissions are promising, but open-label, small and uncontrolled against rituximab. $788M cap; the 1000 mg cohort in 2027 is the next test.
ANNX: Single-infusion tanruprubart improved EQ-VAS at week 1 (p=0.0089) in a Ph3 of 241; the EU MAA is under review and the US BLA is guided Q4 2026. $788M cap vs $213M cash; IVIG is the standard of care.
COGT: Three positive Phase 3s (SUMMIT p=0.0002) feed PDUFAs on Nov 30, Dec 30 and Jun 2027. The $5.2B cap already assumes a successful launch against Sanofi's approved Ayvakit.
PRQR: First clinical validation of Axiomer RNA editing (dose-dependent bile acid changes in healthy volunteers) is real, but patient efficacy waits for the mid-2027 Ph2. Cash is 71% of the $169M cap.
MESO: Ryoncil FY2026 net revenue of $115.2M (net loss $57.5M) is real, but a $1.6B cap is about 14x sales. The LVAD BLA filing and mid-2027 low-back-pain Ph3 readout are the swing factors; MSC efficacy remains contested.
TTRX: A $261M cap against $10M cash and ~6.5 quarters of runway makes the Q1 2027 Ph2 AD topline a financing event as much as a data one. Interim EASI-90 was 44.4% vs 30.4% vehicle (n=50).
ALMS: Two positive Ph3s (PASI90 68.0%/62.1% at wk 24 vs apremilast) and a Q4 2026 NDA sit behind a $665M cap, after the Sep 1 SLE miss cut the stock 57%. Sotyktu is the bar, with no head-to-head; cash is $431M.
FATE: The market ascribes ~$20M ($159M cap less $139M cash) to FT819, now in the potentially registrational RECLAIM-LN trial. Kyverna leads in CD19 CAR-T and runway is ~5 quarters.
SCYX: BREXAFEMME royalties are negligible ($0.2M license revenue in Q2) and MARIO Ph3 was terminated, so $71M cash at 2x $34M cap is cheap for a reason until early assets read out.
CRMD: Q2'26 revenue was $101.9M (DefenCath $66.1M, Melinta $35.8M) vs a $383M cap and $355M cash. REZZAYO sNDA action in Q1 2027 is a catalyst; DefenCath concentration and $145M debt temper it.
DTIL: First paired-biopsy evidence of cccDNA inactivation, 47-69% HBsAg cuts and no DLTs to 0.8 mg/kg, but still Ph1/2 in HBV. A $215M cap against $82M cash and $23M debt leaves little margin for error.
TVGN: Financing and listing risk swamp any Long COVID pivot: $1M of cash on a $37M cap, a Nasdaq compliance notice and n=12 uncontrolled Ph1 data.
VXRT: A pill norovirus vaccine shows GI.1 antibodies +141% and GII.4 +94% in Ph1, but immunogenicity is not protection. Moderna is roughly 1-2 years ahead in Ph3; $66M cash backs an $88M cap.
BEAM: BEAM-302 lifted total AAT to 12.4 uM at 60mg (29 patients, no SAEs) and is in pivotal dosing; risto-cel BLA could come by YE26. $2.3B cap backed by $1.0B cash, about 9.6 quarters of runway.
SION: Trading at 0.6x cash after SION-719 flatlined on sweat chloride (-1.0 mmol/L, p=0.7), the stock has a cash floor. SION-451+2222 is Ph1-only, with its Ph2 starting Q1 2027 against Vertex.
SVRA: Molgramostim PDUFA is Nov 22 (Priority Review, no AdCom) after a positive IMPALA-2 Ph3. $130M cash is 3.7 quarters, and aPAP is a small market against a $1.2B cap.
AMPH: Q3 BAQSIMI revenue of $58.8M (+10%) is about 28% of the $208M quarter, but Lilly and Xeris compete and rebate pressure persists. A $1.2B cap carries $613M of debt and an open warning letter.
ASND: YORVIPATH grew 103% to EUR291M and 2026 operating cash flow is guided to at least EUR600M, but the $18B cap already reflects it. YUVIWEL faces entrenched Voxzogo; the Q4 EC decision is a minor event.
PLYX: SOTERIA has Fast Track but only one US site active and no patient dosed; evidence is mouse-only. An $83M cap is about 10x its $8M cash, with 2.7 quarters of runway, so dilution likely precedes data.
MBX: Canvuparatide showed 63% vs 31% responders at wk12 but trails approved YORVIPATH by 1-2 years. $2.6B cap with $482M cash; MBX 4291 obesity data due Q4 2026.
IVA: NATiV3 Ph3 topline is due Q4 2026 and the $272M cash funds the company through it. Ph2b showed fibrosis improvement of 48% vs 23%, but Rezdiffra is already approved, so this is a binary readout.
KLRA: The positive China Ph3s belong to partner Hengrui, not Kailera's own program, whose KaiNETIC Ph3 reads mid-2028. Cash of $1.04B is 64% of the cap, but tirzepatide and Structure's oral GLP-1 are ahead on proof.
RANI: RaniPill delivered >150% of SC bioavailability in 30 volunteers, but weight-loss efficacy is unproven and Rybelsus and orforglipron are ahead. $45M cash is 5.6 quarters of runway; Nasdaq bid risk near $1.
SRPT: Q3 net product revenue was $323.8M (PMO $240.3M, Elevidys $83.5M), and $999M cash exceeds $857M debt at a $1.6B cap. The ambulatory-only label with boxed liver warning limits it; Dyne is closing in.
BNTC: All 9 treated OPMD patients met responder criteria with no SAEs, in a disease with no approved gene therapy. Small-n data; $176M cash is 42% of the $423M cap, and pivotal start is mid-2027.
RAPP: RAP-219 is in Ph3 for focal epilepsy with runway through 2029 on about $815M pro forma cash against a $1.4B cap. The 72% seizure reduction came from an open-label Ph2a of 27 patients.
FLNA: Repurposed Cassava drug w mouse-only TSC data is a value trap; lifting clinical hold does not create a human signal, even w cash ($51M) at 2.2x $23M cap.
ALKS: Takeda's ORZEYFUL was approved Aug 5, so alixorexton (Ph3 topline from mid-2027) is a follower in orexin agonists. The $8.2B cap rests on ~$480M of quarterly revenue from the existing business.
ABOS: ALTITUDE-AD, a 542-patient Ph2, reads out in late 2026 for a lower-ARIA anti-amyloid backed only by Ph1 plaque reduction of 20-25%; $79M cash w 2.9 quarters of runway makes this a binary.
CGTX: SHIMMER (n=130) met safety, but the 86% slowing on NPI-12 missed significance (p=0.0545). Ph3 has no start date, CervoMed's neflamapimod is ahead, and cash is $32M against a $61M cap.
GANX: Uncontrolled Ph1b biomarker data (n=21) and 2.9 quarters of cash against a Ph2 that slipped to 1Q27 and is unfunded; IND clearance is real, but next event is a raise.
OKYO: Urcosimod has no approved NCP competitor, and Ph2a showed VAS -5.5 vs -2.75, but in only 6 vs 6 patients. NEPTUNE Ph3 is enrolling, with $21M cash against a $62M cap, so a raise looks likely.
NTRB: Preclinical abuse-deterrent fentanyl patch with no efficacy data and the pivotal HAP study not yet started. A $71M cap against $3M cash and about 6 quarters of runway makes funding the issue.
DFTX: Three positive Ph3s for DT120 (GAD HAM-A -5.4 and -5.1; MDD MADRS -8.1) plus Breakthrough in MDD, and about $1.05B cash. NDA is due 1H 2027, though a $4.1B cap already credits much of that.
HELP: Ph3 APPROACH hit at week 6 (MADRS -7.6 vs placebo, remission 50.9% vs 18.2%, n=222). Cash of $171M against a $583M cap and 4.8 quarters of runway leave a gap before the second Ph3, EMBRACE, reads 4Q 2027.
NERV: Roluperidone's confirmatory Ph3 (about 380 patients, Part A topline 2H 2027) follows a prior FDA rejection. A $166M cap with $77M cash, $60M debt and 0.6 quarters of runway means a raise comes first.
APMD: First oral OSA combo with positive SynAIRgy (n=646) and LunAIRo Ph3s, and a PDUFA date of Feb 28 2027. $352M cash backs a $678M cap; dry mouth, insomnia and payer coverage remain open issues.
VOGX: Gut-restricted SGLT1 inhibitor with two completed Ph2s in PBH and $82M cash against a $214M cap. EMERGE Ph2b reads out only in 2H 2027, and Amylyx's Ph3-positive avexitide is well ahead.
TLPH: 70-patient CRRT Ph3, 75% enrolled, is entire story, and thin cash looks tight to finish it; a $53M cap, but financing comes first.
HROW: Q3 revenue of $99.3M and a reaffirmed $350-365M guide show VEVYE working (+75%). But $293M of debt against $75M of cash and a crowded dry-eye field leave the $1.1B cap with little margin for error.
WWB: Interim POLARIS-1 shows FEV1 up to +267 mL (p=0.033, n=147), with no head-to-head vs Tezspire. A $1.0B cap is rich for interim data; week-24 primary is 1H27 and Ph3 topline not until 1H29.
AGIO: Cash of $907M covers half the $1.8B cap, and approved PKD/thalassemia sales run $55M a quarter. SCD PDUFA is Feb 1, 2027 (extended); Hb response 40.6% vs 2.9% but no pain-crisis win, with Novo's etavopivat following.
CLLS: Preclinical only after a Sep 2026 pivot to in vivo APOC3 editing, with ~76% TG cut in mice and human data not until 2H 2027. Cash of $147M tops the $105M cap, but $77M of debt offsets some of that.
ATRA: Tab-cel is EU-approved with ~50% ORR in EBV+ PTLD, and the US PDUFA is Mar 31 2027. But cash is about $10M against $41M debt and a $65M cap, so going-concern and dilution risk dominate.
SLS: REGAL Ph3 hit OS (24.0 vs 14.7 mo, HR 0.59, p=0.035, n=126), but a $3.9B cap prices in a lot for a single-trial AML vaccine ahead of a 1H27 BLA. Cash was $135M at 9/30, before a proposed $150M public offering; expect dilution.
LEGN: Carvykti is the best-selling myeloma CAR-T, with CARTITUDE-4 PFS HR 0.26 and $853M cash against a $3.1B cap. The 47% 12-month drop reflects early deaths, CEO turnover and J&J funding friction.
CCCC: Cemsidomide showed 53% ORR at the RP2D in heavily pretreated myeloma (median 7 priors). Combo data are due mid-2027; cash is 76% of the $361M cap, but BMS's CELMoDs set the bar.
ATNM: ATNM-400 is a preclinical Ac-225 prostate asset w no human data facing entrenched Pluvicto, and market gives it little ($52M cap vs $42M cash); wait for IND.
CMPX: Trades below cash ($119M cap vs $163M) after FDA asked on Sep 22 for an OS trial before a BLA. The randomized win (ORR 18.0% vs 5.3%, PFS 4.7 vs 2.6 mo) is overlooked, though OS missed amid 54% crossover.
ONCY: ~30% ORR vs ~14% historical in anal cancer and FDA alignment on a pivotal are real, but $5M cash against $55M cap makes financing first event; high-risk, funding-gated.
EXEL: A $16B cap with zanzalintinib's mCRC OS gain modest (HR 0.80) against regorafenib, Lonsurf combo and fruquintinib. The Mar 3, 2027 PDUFA looks largely priced; Exelixis earns $605M a quarter and holds $1.4B cash.
CGON: PIVOT-006 Ph3 cut recurrence 68% (HR 0.32, no Gr3+ TRAEs) and SUO is Dec 2. Yet the $7.1B cap, up 81% in 12 months, already reflects it, and the BLA is not complete until March 2027.
ENGN: A $132M cap vs $266M cash (debt $33M) discounts weak durability (~25% at 12 mo) against cretostimogene and Anktiva. 56% any-time CR and a Q4 2026 BLA start give cash-backed upside.
CADL: The Ph3 in localized prostate cancer (n=745) cut recurrence or death 30% (HR 0.70, p=0.0155), and 38-39% on the prostate-cancer-specific measure, with SPA, RMAT and Fast Track. The BLA slipped to mid-2027 on assay work; a $450M cap vs $203M cash rests on one pivotal trial.
ARVN: The $443M cap is below $559M cash (0.8x), with no debt. ARV-102 shows >50% LRRK2 knockdown in CSF for 28 days, but clinical benefit is unproven and Denali's LRRK2 inhibitor is further along.
LONA: ELAINE-1 missed significance (HR 0.70, p=0.14) and thin runway means a raise first, but w $33M cap below its $51M cash into a 2H27 Ph3 it is a cash-backed option on ~13mo combo mPFS.
CGEN: MAIA-ovarian, a randomized placebo-controlled maintenance study (62 pts), reports by end of Q1 2027. Cash of $118M covers 61% of the $193M cap, which cushions the downside; a show-me binary.
FTH: PIK-201 Ph2 showed 33% confirmed ORR (12/36), 7.4 mo mPFS and 64% Gr3+ TRAEs, single-arm. $175M cash against a $241M cap gives support while FDA feedback on Ph3 design is awaited.
PDSB: A 71% ORR and 80% 24-mo survival in a small NCI-run MSS CRC Ph2 is unconfirmed. With $15M cash (about 3.6 quarters) vs a $67M cap and PDS0101 Ph3 discontinued, wait for the Ph3 protocol filing.
BBOT: BBO-8520 posts 63% ORR in G12C-naive patients (n=41) and 75% at 500mg QD with pembrolizumab after G12C inhibitors (53% across doses, n=17), but trails Amgen, BMS and Roche on n and follow-up. Cash of $315M exceeds the $159M cap.
BDTX: The $88M cap is below $102M cash while silevertinib shows 60% ORR, 15.0-mo mPFS and 86% CNS ORR (n=43 at 200mg). 150mg data are unreported, and ArriVent's firmonertinib (16-mo mPFS) sets the bar.
ZLAB: Zoci's 1L SCLC Ph1 (ORR 81.8%, n=33) is strong, but the $2.6B cap also covers a China business booking $108M a quarter. Tarlatamab sets the bar and the DLLEVATE interim is 2H27.
IOVA: Q3 revenue of $122M (+80% YoY, ~60% gross margin) and an HLA-unrestricted label back a $3.5B cap. Cash is $382M, so the 2027 NSCLC sBLA and ex-US approvals must extend the ramp.
NTHI: NEO100's 48.9% 6-month PFS vs a 20% benchmark (n=24, single-arm) is encouraging, but $2M cash and about 0.4 quarters of runway put dilution ahead of the FDA meeting on a $113M cap.
IMNM: RINGSIDE (n=156) cut progression risk 84% and met every key endpoint; PDUFA is Apr 28, 2027. Nirogacestat is the incumbent, and $462M cash against a $2.0B cap funds the launch into 2028.
MIST: At $52M vs $145M cash (and $143M debt), the market treats the CARDAMYST launch as a failure: Q3 sales were $1.0M, +73% q/q, against free off-label propafenone. Q3 net loss was $25.8M.
LRMR: BLA submitted Nov 16 on a frataxin surrogate, with approval targeted mid-2027. Cash of $129M and 4.7 quarters of runway point to a raise, and Skyclarys is the entrenched incumbent.
LQDA: Q3 YUTREPIA sales of $222.7M (+31% q/q) and $140.5M adj. EBITDA show a strong launch, and the stock has roughly doubled in 12 months. The $5.0B cap is exposed to the court remedy on PH-ILD and to Tyvaso DPI's entrenched share.
PVLA: SELVA (n=49) showed a 2.13-pt IGA gain (p<0.001) and Priority Review sets a Feb 28, 2027 PDUFA, so approval looks likely. A $2.3B cap, up 60% in 12 months, assumes QTORIN can hold orphan pricing vs ~$100/yr generic sirolimus.
ABEO: Q3 ZEVASKYN sales of $13.5M (+18% q/q; 15 treatments since launch, 8 QTCs) against a $161M cap only 1.2x cash. Surgical-graft logistics and Krystal's more convenient VYJUVEK limit the ramp.
PTHS: ZELSUVMI revenue of $15.4M (+45% QoQ) against $28M cap; w $32M cash and $30M drawn on its credit facility, capital structure is whole debate.
FDMT: 4D-150 cut aflibercept injections 78% over two years (n=45), and Ph3 4FRONT-1 reads Q2 2027. With $375M cash and ~6.7 quarters of runway, a financing could come first; TKI implants are the rival.
BLTE: First-ever Stargardt candidate (36% lesion-growth cut, p=0.0033) has priority review and a Feb 12 2027 PDUFA. The $6.6B cap leans heavily on the unproven geographic atrophy Ph3, not the small Stargardt market.
ALDX: Three CRLs on field-trial reproducibility and no resubmission date make cash only real asset ($65M, 1.8x $36M cap); avoid until FDA dispute resolves.
SPRY: neffy revenue is growing but payers are slow: no new formulary wins in the Jul 2026 cycle. $138M cash vs $197M debt on a $361M cap; the CSU Ph2b interim (Q1 2027) is the offset. Down 61% in 12 months.
NTLA: Ph3 HAELO hit and the BLA has priority review (PDUFA Mar 10 2027, no adcom). The $1.4B cap carries $615M cash, which must fund a launch of a one-time therapy against monthly injectables; durability is still to be proven.
AGMB: A $294M cap is roughly covered by $288M cash, buying an oral GI-restricted ALK5 inhibitor entering Ph2b in fibrostenotic Crohn's. Efficacy in strictures is unproven and no readout is guided; no drug is approved for strictures.
PALI: Its gut-restricted PDE4 inhibitor has $114M cash, enough to reach the Q4 2027 Ph2b UC readout. Evidence so far is a five-patient open-label signal, against approved agents like upadacitinib; the cap is $219M.
VTVT: CATT1 Ph3 is fully enrolled (166 randomized), topline mid-2027, with no Ph3 efficacy data yet. A $220M cap with $77M cash and 18+ quarters of runway makes this a binary readout.
JBIO: JADE101 cut IgA ~70% in 32 healthy volunteers, but patient data wait for the Q2 2027 JUNIPER interim, and atacicept is already approved. $476M cash cushions a $1.3B cap.
GENB: Golukibart has Ph1 biomarker data (n=96) but no exacerbation data; Ph3 SOLAIRIA-1/2 topline is 2H 2027. $1.4B cap, $404M cash, and approved Tezspire sets the bar.
RNAC: AURORA Ph3 gMG topline is due Q1 2027 on an SPA-agreed design; $208M cap vs $123M cash (5.2 quarters). Retreatment gave -6.6 MG-ADL at month 12, but in only 5 patients.
HCM: China NMPA decisions on sovleplenib in wAIHA (Ph3 durable Hb response 66.0%) and ITP are due by year-end. Cash is $1.4B against a $2.6B cap, but with no US filing the read-through is limited.
ROIV: LISRAYA's Aug 27 dermatomyositis approval and $4.2B cash support a $28B cap, but Immunovant's two TED Ph3s failed and a CLE Ph2 missed. Graves' and MG readouts in 2027 carry the rest.
ELDN: Zero biopsy-proven rejections after month 6 and eGFR 71 vs 58 are strong, but the ~600-patient Ph3 needs funding. Cash is $70M with about 3.3 quarters of runway against a $238M cap.
IMA: Ph2b slipped a full year to Q4 2027 after enrollment tripled and only efficacy data are uncontrolled, so $46M cap against $117M cash is not enough of a discount.
ARQT: Q3 ZORYVE revenue of $143.9M (+45% YoY) and guidance of $535-545M are strong, but a $3.4B cap is about 6x guidance. Infant AD PDUFA is Feb 23 2027; generics and Opzelura limit pricing.
IMVT: D2T RA Ph2 hit at 600 mg (ACR20 92.5% vs 75.6%) but 300 mg did not separate, cutaneous lupus Ph2b missed, and Vyvgart leads. A $6.9B cap argues for waiting on the 2027 Ph3s.
INVA: Q3 revenue was $106.1M: GSK royalties $58.1M plus $43.3M US product sales (+45%, on track for $150M+ in 2026). The $1.3B cap vs $581M cash hinges on royalty duration and a holding-co discount.
VALN: VALOR showed >70% efficacy but its lower CI bound dipped just below the 20% threshold; EMA validated the MAA (Aug 2026) and Pfizer is aligning the FDA path. A $536M cap vs $141M cash and $244M debt looks fair.
ALGS: Pevifoscorvir, Aligos' HBV capsid inhibitor w FDA Fast Track, finished Phase 2 enrollment w topline due late Q3 2027; $31M cash is about 3x $10M cap.
DCOY: Hamster-only data (~4-log viral reduction), no human trial until 2027 and 3.5 quarters of runway make this a melting ice cube, not a floor, though cash exceeds $3M cap.
PROK: Ph2 (n=24) showed a 78% improvement in eGFR decline and FDA accepts slope for accelerated approval. A $315M cap sits against $142M cash, but 3.7 quarters of runway is thin around the PROACT-1 topline.
KMDA: FY25 revenue $180.5M (+12%) and net income $20.2M (+40%); H1'26 revenue $100.2M (+13%). Inhaled AAT was discontinued, so the $469M cap (2.6x sales, $75M cash) rides on KEDRAB-led execution.
TRVI: First-in-indication for IPF cough with a clean Ph2b (n=165), but opioid-class perception vs P2X3 rivals is open. A $2.1B cap already prices in success; LAKE re-estimation due early Q1 2027.
KRRO: KRRO-121 has mouse and NHP data plus healthy-volunteer dosing since Sept 2026; UCD patients dose 1H27 with interim data 2H27. A $227M cap on a preclinical-stage platform, with $125M cash.
BMEA: COVALENT-211 (Q1 2027) must be financed before it reads out, given a pulled September offering and runway only into Q2 2027; cap is $42M.
BMRN: Diversified and profitable, with FY26 revenue guided to $3.33-3.43B. The $11B cap carries $4.2B debt and rising Ascendis competition, so the Feb 28, 2027 Voxzogo FDA action and HCH sNDA matter.
SPRB: TA-ERT normalized CSF HS-NRE and stabilized Bayley-III cognition over 6 years (n=22, natural-history comparison); BLA guided December. $88M cash vs a $121M cap, $15M debt, 5.9 quarters of runway.
ARCT: ARCT-032 missed protocol FEV1 (post-hoc Day-42 signal only), so a $237M cap against $185M cash looks fairly priced. 12-week Cohort 4 data in Q2 2027 precede a Ph3 decision.
ALT: Cash of $480M exceeds the $320M cap after a 66% 12-month slide, so the pipeline is priced as an option. The 24-week fibrosis endpoint was missed, MASH is crowded with Rezdiffra approved, and Ph3 data are not due until 2029.
GPCR: Oral GLP-1 with ~16% placebo-adjusted weight loss at 44 weeks in Ph2b and Ph3 dosing. Cash of $1.24B, about 91% of the cap, funds through 2028, but Lilly's orforglipron sets the bar.
VERU: QUALITY (n=168) preserved lean mass on semaglutide (p=0.002) and cap is $36M, but going-concern flags and an add-on role make financing gate.
SLDB: Next-gen capsid lifted micro-dystrophin from 58% to ~100% by Day 360 and Ph3 is dosing, but the $1.0B cap already prices in a lot with Ph3 data years out. A late-Q4 FDA meeting on accelerated approval is the test.
PEPG: FREEDOM2-DM1 showed 46.5% splicing correction vs 6.8% placebo with no SAEs, but in only 8 patients with inconclusive PROs. US partial hold persists; $105M cash is 39% of the $269M cap. OLE data Jan 2027.
BHVN: Ono ($80M upfront) and SK ($350M) deals ease $164M cash vs $264M debt, and runway is short. Troriluzole in SCA has a 1Q27 PDUFA, Graves' Ph3 is just starting, and the cap is $2.1B.
ABCL: The positive Ph2 (83% vs 33% hot-flash reduction) is already in a $3.6B cap, and the stock is up 136% in 12 months. Veoza and elinzanetant are approved and Ph3 starts in 2027, so upside needs replication.
HRMY: WAKIX grew 30% to a record ~$261M in Q2, and $1.1B cash is 54% of the $1.9B cap (debt $150M). The open question is orexin-agonist erosion; the Apr 1, 2027 pitolisant GR PDUFA extends the franchise.
ACOG: Zunveyl Q3 revenue was $7.8M (+30% QoQ, +230% YoY) with 1,639 prescribers (+22%). The question is whether premium pricing holds against sub-$5 generic donepezil; cash is $38M with no debt.
CRVO: Best signal in DLB (54% lower CDR-SB worsening risk, p=0.0037), but Ph3 now depends on a partner and $25M cash lasts 4 quarters; $23M cap is cheap only if financing does not eat it.
TSHA: The pivotal REVEAL trial is fully dosed (17 patients) with no treatment-related SAEs, and $423M cash covers the 1H27 interim. Neurogene's NGN-401 is ahead on enrollment in Rett gene therapy.
MIRA: No human efficacy yet for an oral ketamine analog in a field of failed CIPN programs, w going-concern language and a Ph2a not yet dosed; $8M cash is 29% of $28M cap.
HRTX: Fragile: Q2'26 revenue of $37.7M missed management's own plan and 2026 guidance was withdrawn. The $51M cap faces $126M debt and $23M cash, and the CorMedix asset sale closes Q1 2027 pending a vote.
VTGN: Two straight Ph3 misses (PALISADE-3 and -4) and 2.4 quarters of runway say cash will be spent on another try, not returned, despite $32M being 4.6x $7M cap.
NRXP: Approval is in hand (Oct 2026) with first ketamine shipments by Jan 2027. The test is a rolling NRX-100 NDA by year-end, after repeated delays since 2024, on only $27M cash against a $102M cap.
MPLT: Trades at about 0.9x its $463M cash on a $415M cap after a 55% 12-month slide. ZEPHYR met its primary (-4.5 PANSS, p=0.015), but ZEPHYR-2 reads in 2028, behind approved Cobenfy.
LTGO: Onzotrigine hit its Ph2b primary (n=343, NEJM Jul 2026) and $401M cash is ample, but an $835M cap prices in success while Vertex's approved Journavx leads. Ph3 topline is 2H 2027.
CUVL: Scenesse is the only approved EPP drug, with roughly $60-90M revenue and profits. EV is about $77M after $174M cash, so the Dec 2026 vitiligo Ph3 is cheap optionality; Disc's bitopertin is the threat.
ALNY: Amvuttra did $1.13B in Q3 (total TTR $1.15B, +59%) on 2026 TTR guidance of $4.2-4.5B. A $21B cap against tafamidis generics and acoramidis leaves the stock priced for sustained leadership.
ETRA: The market pays only ~$119M over $403M cash for ipsoprubart: 100% 8-week survival vs ~50% historical in n=12. But SURPASS is single-arm with an external control regulators may not accept; enrollment ends 2H 2027.
ASPE: Open-label data (n=15) show no graft-induced dyskinesia and gains at 18-24 months, with RMAT and Fast Track. Only a few high-dose patients have long follow-up and sham effects are large in PD, so Ph3 design feedback matters.
COAG: Zero treated bleeds in 8 of 9 evaluable VWD patients over 28 days is early, single-dose data. The $1.8B cap already prices in success, at 4x the $430M cash. Next data at EAHAD Feb 2027.
NRIX: Bexobrutideg posted 83% ORR and 22.1-month mPFS (n=47) in CLL, and Roche funding runs into 2H 2029. At a $1.7B cap it is priced on Phase 1 data ahead of a Phase 3 vs pirtobrutinib; BeiGene's degrader competes.
ESLA: $17M micro-cap CAR-T w eye-catching but tiny (n=5) early lymphoma remissions and only ~$0.1M cash - promotional and high-risk.
KURA: Komzifti is second to market behind Syndax's revumenib, with Q3 revenue of $13.9M and 420+ prescriptions. ASH orals on Dec 12 and Dec 14 on frontline combos matter; cash is 77% of the $637M cap with ~8 quarters of runway.
ADPT: clonoSEQ ran 39,587 tests (+46%) and Q3 MRD revenue hit $72.6M, with positive net income and raised guidance. A $4.5B cap is a rich multiple for this revenue base; the MolDX bundle decision is undated.
GERN: IMpactMF in myelofibrosis was stopped Oct 28, leaving Rytelo in LR-MDS, where Q3 revenue was $60.1M (+27% YoY) with $1.4M net income. $339M cash is about half the $686M cap; Germany launches by YE26.
TCRX: Not a data story but a cash discount w ~4 quarters to burn: a preclinical in vivo PRAME/MAGE-A4 pivot after 75% layoff and a paused heme Ph3, at $12M cap vs $100M cash (0.12x).
JAZZ: Ziihera won 1L HER2+ GEA (OS HR 0.65) but sold just $21M in 3Q26 against $1.2B total quarterly revenue. Zepzelca's 2L SCLC LAGOON Ph3 missed OS, though 1L maintenance (IMforte, OS HR 0.73) is unaffected; at a $16B cap, launch pace is upside, not the thesis.
IMRX: Single-arm mOS of 17.3 mo (n=55) with the randomized Ph3 enrolling ahead of plan (~570 pts). Cash of $166M backs much of the $228M cap, but pan-RAS rival daraxonrasib could displace a MEK inhibitor. Topline mid-2028.
CRDF: Randomized ORR of 72% vs 42% (n=18 vs 19) is small but striking. Shares are down 63% in 12 months to a $66M cap vs $34M cash; with 3 quarters of runway, funding the Ph3 is the real issue.
TYRA: Bladder data (79% ORR, 11/14, no Gr3 related AEs) is secondary; the $1.7B cap largely rests on achondroplasia, where BEACH301 data come in 2027. $701M cash funds the work, but the raise dilutes.
RCUS: Casdatifan 2L median PFS of 14.5 mo (n=43) is cross-trial only, and Merck's belzutifan+lenvatinib already has positive Ph3 data. $694M cash plus a $288M raise runs into 2029.
KYNB: FG-3246's 21% composite response is weak, so this is a below-cash value long rather than an efficacy bet; $87M cash is 5.8x $15M cap, so failure is already priced.
GLSI: FLAMINGO-01 is a real Ph3, but the Ph2 was small and the $202M cap rests on just $6M cash, about 1.8 quarters of runway. Funding is the issue; interim is event-driven.
ACRV: Market cap of $63M is below $78M cash, ahead of a Q4 2026 interim on Arms 3+4. Fast Track and no direct CHK1 rival help, but biomarker selection must hold and runway is just 4.9 quarters.
CNTX: 29% confirmed ORR vs ~10% historical in pretreated ovarian cancer w Fast Track is draw, backed by $55M cash, 3.2x $17M cap; Ph1 size and mid-2027 runway are caveats.
NBTX: NANORAY-312 dropped its interim, so the Ph3 final analysis should come sooner with fewer events. But a $1.5B cap against $126M cash rests on single-arm Ph1 data (mOS 23 vs ~12 mo historical).
CVM: Striking 73% vs 45% five-year OS in a PD-L1-low subgroup is post-hoc salvage after broad trial missed, and $2M cash makes 212-patient confirmatory Ph3 a financing question first.
CBIO: CR-001 has no human efficacy data, and a $617M cap sits on a PD-1xVEGF fast follower trailing ivonescimab by 14-16 months. Cash of $289M; ASCEND proof-of-concept data are due Q1 2027.
BYSI: DUBLIN-3's HR 0.82 comes w $26M cap, but w $8M cash and ~3.6 quarters of runway, confirmatory DUBLIN-4 is a financing event before it is a data event.
PBYI: NERLYNX Q3 revenue was $54.1M (+4%), FY26 net income guided to $20-22M, $109M cash and no debt. A mature base facing generics and weak alisertib signals in SCLC leave the $390M cap exposed.
REPL: Tudriqev's launch is the test: IGNYTE showed 24.2% ORR and 14.1-month mDOR, approval followed two CRLs, and first sales come in Dec 2026. The $2.4B cap vs $308M cash follows a doubling in the share price.
KZIA: TNBC Ph1b showed 5 of 6 evaluable responders (1 CR, 4 PR), but n is tiny, GBM missed its primary, and enrollment runs to Jul 2027. $40M cash against an $87M cap.
INBX: Ozekibart roughly doubled PFS (5.52 vs 2.66 mo, HR 0.479) with a PDUFA of Apr 14, 2027. Yet the $1.2B cap is 6x cash, debt is $277M, and a hepatotoxicity signal and rare-tumor market limit the case.
KARD: Promising early signals in an area with no good options, but open-label and uncontrolled. Plenty of cash and a strong team; the verdict waits for the randomized Ph2b in 2Q27.
RNA: Trading at less than half of $232M cash ($105M cap), but ATR-1072 only just dosed its first patient and has no human data until 2H27. Cash funds through 2028; the discount looks justified until proof of concept.
TECX: Binary APEX Ph2 (n=191, 72% enriched CpcPH) reads out by end of Jan 2027. A $413M cap is 1.8x cash, but sotatercept's CADENCE PVR win (p=0.004) in the same population narrows TX45's window.
SGMT: Denifanstat won a 480-patient China Ph3 in acne and cash of $258M funds the US Ph3 to mid-2029. But US AURORA reads only in 2H 2027 and must beat cheap generic isotretinoin, so execution has to deliver.
INMB: MINDFuL missed its clinical primary (biomarker hit only, p=0.0028), and going-concern risk plus a partner-needed Ph2b/3 make this financing-gated option value; cash is 64% of $33M cap.
MDWD: VALUE Ph3 enrollment is running slower than planned, with the sample-size reassessment due end Q1 2027. Cash is only $28M against a $176M cap, so funding is the issue; EscharEx still needs VLU proof.
KLRS: Cap is 0.4x cash for an aflibercept-based TH103 w +10 letters in n=13, but AXPAXLI, DURAVYU and 4D-150 are all at Ph3; cash buys option until MAD data in mid-2027.
OCGN: OCU400 Ph3 (n=140) is fully enrolled with topline in Q1 2027, a clear catalyst for a $261M cap. But $84M cash against $132M debt gives ~5 quarters of runway, so a raise looks likely.
LENZ: Cash of $197M exceeds the $120M cap, and VIZZ sold $2.6M in Q3 (+~50% q/q) on >38,000 paid Rx. The debate is cash-pay adoption, with an interim CEO from 12/1/26 and a marketing reorganization under way.
DBVT: VITESSE Ph3 hit (46.6% vs 14.8% placebo) and the BLA is filed with Breakthrough status. But $166M cash covers about 3.2 quarters of a $646M cap; dilution is a risk until the FDA filing decision.
CLDX: Two positive CSU Ph3s (n=1,939) with 42-55% complete response in omalizumab-refractory patients, and $650M cash backing a 2027 BLA. The $2.2B cap leaves the debate on share vs Novartis' remibrutinib.
STTK: SL-325 is a DR3 antagonist chasing TL1A, where Merck's tulisokibart leads by 2+ years in late Ph3. Ph2b Crohn's data are not due until 1H28, yet the stock is up 133% in 12 months to $854M vs $196M cash.
EQ: EQ504 only just began Ph1 SAD/MAD in healthy volunteers, with proof-of-mechanism data in H1 2027. Cash of $53M is about 41% of the $129M cap, and UC is crowded with approved agents.
SABS: Only four treated Ph1 patients, but 3 of 4 preserved C-peptide, and the Ph2b has Fast Track. $205M cash runs through 2028, past the 2H 2027 topline; the $622M cap already credits a lot.
AUPH: Q3 LUPKYNIS sales of $79.4M and a raised $325-330M revenue guide are solid, with $487M cash, but a $2.1B cap is over 6x revenue and zetomipzomib is early. A balanced setup.
UPB: Ph2 VALIANT (n=478) cut exacerbations 56% at 100 mg q12w (p<0.001), yet the cap is $119M vs $207M cash. Cash funds only through 2027, so the ~1,500-patient Ph3 starting Q1 2027 needs a raise or partner.
VOR: Telitacicept's UPSTREAM MG Ph3 reads out 1H 2027 and decides the case: China data show -7.5 MG-ADL at wk 48, but global replication is unproven and FcRn and complement drugs are approved. $1.8B cap, $482M cash.
LKFT: Early Ph1b data are strong (ITP 18/20 responders, AIHA 9/9, grade 1 CRS in 18%) but follow-up is short. The $2.3B cap is below $2.5B of cash; the ASH poster on Dec 13 is the next test.
CABA: The $188M cap sits below $299M of cash, despite durable drug-free responses in myositis (5/6 at 16 wks, all maintained). Registrational topline is 2H 2027, but runway is about 7 quarters.
QTTB: Cash of $290M roughly equals the $299M cap, so the AA program is priced as nearly free. Open-label n=33 data (35.3% SALT reduction) look JAK-like; placebo-controlled proof and Ph3 are still ahead.
MLTX: HS BLA filed Sep 30 with 67.2% HiSCR75 at 52 weeks, and teen data accepted as pivotal. But sonelokimab did not beat approved bimekizumab head-to-head, and $499M cash sits against $100M debt.
ORKA: Week-28 PASI90 of 87.3% off drug is strong and $1.2B cash funds through BLA. Yet an $8.2B cap, up 241% in 12 months, assumes durability holds; Dec 52-week data face approved IL-23s.
ENLV: Randomized Ph1/2a hit (47% pain reduction, p=0.0001) w RMAT, and $25M cap, but $6M cash and a crypto-treasury pivot add risk.
ARMP: Breakthrough designation (Sep 14) and an FDA-aligned Ph3 superiority design are real, yet $18M cash vs $222M debt and ~2.7 quarters of runway make a raise a precondition to dosing.
SIGA: Approved smallpox franchise with $116M cash against a $205M cap. BARDA 19C is complete and Canada adds up to ~$15M, so timing of a new US contract is the story; mpox Ph2 missed and the EU dropped that label.
PCVX: OPUS-1 hit non-inferiority on 28 shared serotypes and superiority on 3 unique ones, though 3 and 12F cleared only the historical bar vs PCV21. A $9.9B cap prices in success; BLA is 1H 2028 against Merck and Pfizer.
PGEN: Papzimeos is the first approved RRP therapy and the company turned a $35.8M profit in Q3 on $72.9M revenue (+37% QoQ). Thin $51M cash and the EMA review are the swing factors for a $1.7B cap.
AKBA: Vafseo grew from $15.8M in Q1 to $21.3M in Q2 and the VOICE interim was positive. $159M cash exceeds the $125M cap against $52M debt, but the 12/31/26 TDAPA price reset is the key test.
MREO: Setrusumab raised BMD in both Ph3s but missed on fractures, endpoint that matters; $44M cap near $36M cash is a shell w an unfunded alvelestat Ph3 and a case on secondary data.
UTHR: Two positive Ph3 TETON trials back the Tyvaso IPF sNDA, with FDA action due late April 2027. A $25B cap leaves little room for error, and Merck's sotatercept pressures the PAH base.
PLX: Profitable, with H1'26 net income of $22.1M and 2026 revenue guided to $78-83M. The PRX-115 gout upside is early, with Ph2 data due 2H 2027 against entrenched Krystexxa.
IONS: First approved sHTG drug (TG down up to 72%), with 2026 revenue guided to $875-900M and EU decision due Q4 2026. The pelacarsen miss and Arrowhead's mid-2027 plozasiran weigh; $4.6B cap against $1.9B cash.
IRON: APOLLO Ph3 met on PPIX (-41.4%, p<0.0001) and pain-free time (+12.2 hours). NDA resubmission by YE2026, FDA decision mid-2027, after an earlier CRL. $683M cash backs the $3.5B cap.
MNPR: Pooled FoCus data (n=266) show UWDRS-III p=0.006 vs p=0.435 for standard chelation, though the neuro benefit is post hoc. Rolling NDA began Jul 22 and completes within weeks. Cap $620M, cash $129M.
NAMS: First global approval (EC, Sep 21) plus a 21% MACE signal (HR 0.79) and LDL-C -33% in BROADWAY. The $2.3B cap is 3.6x its $643M cash; PREVAIL interim (4Q26) and RUBENS (~YE26) are the near-term tests.
GALT: FDA agreed a traditional pathway in MASH cirrhosis, but NAVIGATE missed significance (p=0.13) and $12M cash funds only to June 2027. Financing is the central issue for a $309M cap.
WVE: Cash of $431M against a $586M cap means the pipeline (DMD at 7.8% mean dystrophin, HD, RNA-editing AATD) is valued at only ~$155M. Q4 multidose data and a $12M GSK milestone are the near tests.
IBIO: AI-engineered anti-myostatin entering Ph1 w safety/PK data in Q1 2027 has no human efficacy, so cash backing is thesis, not pipeline; cap is 0.6x $75M cash.
RGNX: AFFINITY DUCHENNE met its primary endpoint, 93% of patients above 10% micro-dystrophin; BLA due Q1 2027. $492M cap against $251M cash and $186M debt, and external-control data face FDA scrutiny after Elevidys.
IXHL: Its Ph2 (n=121, only 14-41% meaningful responders) trails Apnimed's AD109 and a dose-optimization study delays Ph3; constructive only as cash-backed, at 0.4x its $70M cash.
DRUG: Cash of $225M, no debt, exceeds the $217M cap after a 58% one-month drop, so the open-label Ph2 (73.1% median absence-seizure reduction, 24 pts) is priced as free. The full FDA partial-hold letter, due ~Dec 2, sets the risk.
PRAX: Two NDAs are pending: relutrigine (PDUFA Dec 27) and ulixacaltamide for essential tremor (Jan 29), on Ph3 mADL11 -4.3 vs -1.7. At a $9.1B cap, approval looks largely priced in.
GRCE: CMC-only CRL leaves a Ph3-complete IV nimodipine at $37M cap; $17M cash is 46% of cap, so speed of Type A fix and financing decide it.
ANVS: Oral Alzheimer's drug w an intriguing subgroup signal that needs a proper confirmatory trial; $19M cash vs $32M micro-cap leaves little margin.
ALEC: After the INFRONT-3 failure and a second progranulin miss, value is mostly cash ($139M, 36% of the $383M cap) plus the Genentech-licensed AL050. AL137 first-in-human has slipped to Apr 2027.
NGNE: Embolden is fully dosed (25 pts, 9 responders needed, topline 2H 2027) and $360M cash is 56% of the $640M cap. The Ph1/2 was only n=10, so the pivotal decides it; Taysha's TSHA-102 is the main rival.
DWTX: Nov 30 Ph2b topline (217 enrolled; interim 51% vs 35% responders) is a binary for $33M cap w only 2 quarters of runway; a win re-rates, but financing comes w it.
HALO: Q3 revenue rose 39% to $493.0M and FY26 guidance was raised to $1.860-1.925B. At an $11B cap, with $3.25B debt and unresolved Merck litigation over ENHANZE, much of the strength looks priced in.
NBIX: Ingrezza and Crenessity revenue underpin a $17B cap. Osavampator must repeat SAVITRI's -7.5 MADRS in Ph3 in a crowded adjunctive MDD field (Auvelity, Rexulti, generic Abilify).
AYTU: EXXUA scripts ramp (200 to 920 a month, Jan-Apr), but total revenue fell 33% and breakeven is not reached, so launch pace must outrun dilution; $27M cash exceeds $20M cap.
RVPH: Strong Ph3 (-10.1 PANSS vs placebo, p<0.001) and $22M cash vs $4M cap, but a flagged ~$35M funding gap and a mandatory RECOVER-2 make equity an option on financing.
OBX: OBX-115 posted 67% confirmed ORR (10/15) with no DLTs or ICANS, but n=15 is cross-trial against approved Amtagvi, which earns about $102M a quarter in US sales. A $763M cap against $324M cash looks fair until a larger dataset.
VRXA: VXA-102, a preclinical EpCAM T-cell engager with an IND targeted around 2028, is now the lead, and the FLT3 antibody is offered for partnering. A $148M cap is 3.7x its $40M cash and there is no clinical data yet, so a raise is the likely next step.
INSM: Brinsupri sold $400.1M in Q3 (+29% q/q) and 2026 guidance is $1.35-1.40B, with an Arikayce PDUFA on Jan 28 2027. Even so, a $27B cap sets a high bar and shares are down 38% over 12 months.
TRXB: Freshly IPO'd at a $337M cap with $197M cash, TRB-061 has only Ph1a tolerability data and no efficacy. The ~50-patient Ph1b AD readout in mid-2027 is the first real test in a crowded field.
BBTX: BBT001's Ph1 (n=17, 4-week IV; wk 6 placebo-adjusted EASI-75 64%) is early and not head-to-head with Dupixent. At an $814M cap, 12-week SubQ data are not due until H1 2027, with lock-up expiry near Apr 27.
MGX: Preclinical in vivo hem-A editor w monkey-only data faces Novo's SC prophylaxis first; $140M cash is 5x $28M cap, but value trap until human FVIII data.
GMAB: Up 102% in six months to a $33.4B cap; Rina-S's 45.9% ORR in open-label Ph1/2 is good, but pipeline wins already look capitalized.
CRVS: Soquelitinib's Ph1 AD data (EASI -72% vs -40% placebo, n=72) are strong, but the registrational asset is a ~150-patient PTCL Ph3 with a Q1 2027 futility analysis. $982M cap against $203M cash.
OMER: Q3 YARTEMLEA net sales of $35.9M (+26% QoQ) and $4.7M non-GAAP net income show a working launch. The EU CHMP negative stands and the $1.2B cap is already priced for it; Jan 1 2027 340B reimbursement is next.
XCUR: Burixafor met its mobilization primary (89%), but a $6M cap, $3M cash, going-concern doubt and a Nasdaq equity deficiency make survival, not a supportive-care niche, issue.
ELVN: Ph1b showed 54% MMR in 161 CML patients, and Phase 3 ENABLE-2 starts before YE26. The $3.6B cap is well above $884M cash, with Scemblix and a genericizing market as the backdrop.
CTMX: At $434M the market pays only ~$86M over $348M cash for CX-2051: 32% cORR, 7.1 mo mPFS, 88% DCR (n=56, 10mg/kg) in 3L+ CRC. Needs randomized confirmation; Jan 2027 update sets dose and registrational plan.
ZYME: Ziihera's 1L GEA approval (OS HR 0.65) triggered a $250M Jazz milestone, received in October, plus 10-20% royalties. The $1.8B cap sits against about $350M of cash pro forma for that payment and $600M of non-recourse notes repaid from royalty and YUPELRI cash flows; Q3 royalty revenue was only $2.3M.
ACTU: Randomized 1L pancreatic survival win (HR 0.62, n=233) at a $7M cap, but $4M cash and a going-concern warning make dilution real event; a high-risk lottery ticket.
TNGX: Vopimetostat plus daraxonrasib ORR 82% (18/22), 9-mo PFS 88%, but 40% Gr3 TRAEs and a small sample. BMS, Amgen and AZ also chase PRMT5, and Ph3 only starts 1H 2027 at a $4.1B cap.
URGN: ZUSDURI Q3 revenue of $68.0M (+35% QoQ) and a UGN-103 PDUFA on Jun 14, 2027 support a $1.4B cap. Thin cash of $91M against $189M debt is the main risk.
XNCR: XmAb819 showed 45.5% confirmed ORR (n=11) but 72.1% Gr3+ related AEs, trailing Merck's 52.6% in a similar line. A $2.7B cap on Ph1 data, with Ph3 start only by end 2027.
RADX: RAD101 met its Ph2b endpoint (93% MRI concordance, n=30) and FDA aligned on a ~280-patient Ph3. But cash is $4M with ~1.3 quarters of runway, against a $3.3B cap for a niche imaging market.
ALXO: Evorpacept hit 65.0% ORR vs 26.1% control in CD47-high HER2+ gastric (n=43). The $138M cap is below $153M cash, funded to 1H 2028; ASPEN-09-Breast topline is 2H 2027.
CORT: Lifyorli took $91.4M in Q3 on ROSELLA (mOS 16.0 vs 11.9 mo, HR 0.65), Korlym and its authorized generic grew 19% q/q to $249M, and Cushing's PDUFA is Dec 17. The $8.7B cap already prices a lot.
GNLX: OnPrime Ph3 topline is due by year-end, but $10M cash is 11% of the $92M cap. Oncolytic viruses have an uneven record and mirvetuximab holds the FRa+ ovarian lane; a high-risk binary.
BCAX: Ficerafusp alfa's 48-54% cORR and 21.3-mo mOS in 1L HNSCC compare well with pembrolizumab's 19% ORR, but the data are single-arm. FORTIFI-HN01 interim topline in mid-2027 is the proof; $442M cash backs a $669M cap.
SMMT: The FDA CRL cites no significant OS benefit (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.62-1.01) despite PFS HR 0.52. A $9.8B cap against $630M cash now rests on undated HARMONi-3 and HARMONi-7 results.
NVCT: Ciprocopan, a China-approved oral factor B inhibitor, beat eculizumab (94.6% vs 69.4% transfusion-free). The stock has nearly tripled in 12 months, and the US IND by YE26 must show differentiation from Fabhalta.
MAIA: THIO-101 Part C showed 88% DCR (38/43) in 3L+ NSCLC, which the company says may support an accelerated filing. The cap is $61M, cash $21M, so a raise is needed before Ph3 THIO-104 interim survival in 2027.
MOLN: MP0712 cleared dose level 1 with no dose-limiting events, and dose level 2 is fully recruited. It sits 2-3 years behind approved tarlatamab in DLL3, with efficacy not due until 2027; $69M cash, $103M cap.
EVAX: 75% ORR (n=16) w 92% still responding at 2 years is cheap option value against a $25M cap mostly backed by $18M cash, but a tiny n and Merck/Moderna's mRNA-4157 lead cap conviction.
IDYA: OptimUM-02 (n=313) showed mPFS 6.9 vs 3.1 months (HR 0.42) and the NDA is under RTOR. The $3.1B cap, against $1.15B cash, already credits platform value beyond a small uveal market.
OSTX: Rolling BLA on ~40 single-arm patients (3-yr OS 71.2%) w ~$1M cash and 0.1 quarter of runway; cap is $35M, so avoid.
BBIO: Attruby Q3 revenue of $253.2M (+~$145M y/y) is a real launch, but a $15B cap and $3.4B of debt price in a lot, with tafamidis holding share. BBP-418 PDUFA is Nov 27, then two more Priority Review dates.
TNYA: NYHA improved >=1 class in 5 of 6 evaluable patients and EMA PRIME was granted, yet n=6 is small and AAV durability unproven. With $67M cash and 3.9 quarters of runway, financing likely follows the YE pivotal-design update.
TENX: After the failed LEVEL Ph3 (n=241, p=0.63), the case rests on a nominal subgroup (+26.3m, p=0.011, n=119) and an FDA Type C outcome in Q1 2027. $85M cap vs $114M cash does not make up for that.
MANE: Phase 3 data look solid: +43.9 hairs/cm2 at 12 months (BID) and no treatment-related SAEs. But a $5.3B cap is rich for a branded oral minoxidil facing ~$15/month generics; female Study 306 reads 1H 2027.
DERM: Emrosi revenue reached $9.0M in Q3 (+84% YoY) on ~40k scripts, but cash is $22M against ~$26M of term loans and the auditor flags going-concern doubt. Oracea holds the formulary position.
EOLS: Q3 revenue grew 13% to $78.0M with a fourth straight positive adj. EBITDA quarter and a $330-337M FY guide; Sculpt approval is due by year-end. Botox's ~70% share limits how much share Evolus can win.
OTLK: LYTENAVA won approval in Jul 2026 with ~12-year exclusivity, but runway is about one quarter ($11M cash, $18M debt, $97M cap). Payers can still use off-label Avastin, so funding and uptake are the issues.
IRD: LCA5 Ph3 (8 patients) starts dosing Q4 2026 and BEST1 BIRD-1 reads Q1 2027. Evidence is early, but $89M cash against $35M debt and a $387M cap look balanced; runway is ~4.6 quarters.
PHAT: VOQUEZNA Q3 sales reached $84.7M (+71% YoY) with a second straight quarter of positive operating cash flow; FY26 guidance is $310-325M. EoE Ph2 topline and an FDA exclusivity ruling are due near term.
AQST: Anaphylm was resubmitted after a Jan 2026 CRL on human factors; PDUFA is Mar 16 2027. The $473M cap sits against $90M cash and $51M debt, with SPRY's approved neffy already holding the head start.
SEPN: SEP-479 is in healthy-volunteer Ph1 with data Q1 2027, and its first PTH1R candidate was dropped. A $2.0B cap after a 70% 12-month run leaves little room for error; $565M cash.
EPRX: RESOLVE Ph2b (placebo-controlled) has interim data due in December; the open-label Ph1b/2a showed 66% remission at 36 weeks. At a $565M cap with $126M cash, open-label data leave little room for a miss.
VRDN: LUMVOA did $24.7M in its first quarter on market and SC elegrobart files Q1 2027; $955M cash vs $364M debt. At a $3.7B cap, convenience over entrenched Tepezza has to carry the story.
MGTX: Bota-vec rights are back from J&J, with an EMA filing in Dec 2026 and a BLA in Q1 2027. Cash is $187M against $122M of debt, and the $853M cap already prices in approval, so filings must deliver.
NKTX: Myositis 5/6 and SSc 5/7 responses are early and small. The $93M cap sits below $216M cash with 7.9 quarters of runway, but CAR-T rivals like Adicet's prula-cel keep cash from being the whole case.
CNTB: COPD Ph2 hit (81% fewer treatment failures, p=0.0122) but asthma missed, and a $45M cap on $44M cash w 2.9 quarters of runway means dilution before any Ph3. Avoid.
TGTX: Q3 US BRIUMVI revenue of $232.6M (+52%) and FY26 guidance raised to ~$1B are strong, but an $8.8B cap prices in a lot. SubQ Ph3 topline lands YE2026/early 2027 as ocrelizumab biosimilars enter.
KNSA: Q3 ARCALYST revenue of $286.0M (+58%) and guidance raised to $1.045-1.050B are excellent. But an $8.0B cap is about 7.6x that guidance, and Cardiol's Ph3 and KPL-387 data (2H 2027) loom.
ADMA: Q3 revenue grew only 5% to $141.1M as ASCENIV rose 31% and BIVIGAM fell to $15.4M. Guidance of at least $530M puts the $3.0B cap near 5.6x; the next print needs to hold the 71% gross margin.
KYMR: BROADEN2 Ph2b in ~200 AD patients reads by year-end. A $13B cap vs $1.6B cash already prices KT-621 as an oral dupilumab, so it needs a clean, dupilumab-like result.
ZURA: Cash of $188M exceeds the $136M cap after a 72% one-month drop. The 247-patient HS Ph2 reads in Q4 2026; bimekizumab sets the bar, but cash backing limits the downside.
XBIT: A $56M cap vs $105M cash is a discount for a reason: vilamakitug has no clinical efficacy data in axSpA and trails approved IL-17 agents. The V-SPINE Ph2 is the only test.
ANAB: Jemperli net sales of $365M (+20% YoY) and an Oct rectal cancer approval feed the royalty stream; imsidolimab (a skin-disease drug partnered with Vanda) has a PDUFA on Dec 12. GSK/Tesaro royalty litigation and $257M debt vs $164M cash are the risks.
SPRO: Cash of $108M is ~2x the $55M cap but $103M debt nets that to ~$5M. UTEBZI is approved (GSK-run, $25M milestone received); the SP001 Ph2 in IgG4-RD is not planned until ~Q2 2027.
VIR: Ph3 ECLIPSE 1 (n=124) hit 44% vs 0% undetectable HDV RNA with ALT normalization; one Grade 3 related AE. $898M cash is 58% of the $1.5B cap, with ECLIPSE 2/3 data Q1 2027 and FDA filing mid-2027.
NVAX: The pivot to Matrix-M royalties (high-teens to low-20s % from Sanofi, plus a Pfizer license) has worked so far. But a $1.3B cap already reflects it; a $75M Sanofi milestone is due mid-2027.
ASMB: Assembly holds a 40% US cost/profit share and just received a $75M Gilead fee. With a $464M cap and $314M cash, value awaits Gilead's Ph2 start by end 2026; Gilead controls timing.
UNCY: The NDA resubmission was accepted Oct 21 2026 after a CRL citing only manufacturing; PDUFA is ~Mar 25 2027. Efficacy is not the issue, but it is a second CRL on the same deficiency; $61M cash vs a $103M cap.
EDSA: Positive Ph3 ARDS mortality result (24% vs 33%, p<0.001, n=278) at a $28M cap below $33M cash after an 88% drop; open question is whether FDA accepts it or demands a confirmatory trial.
AVLN: AP01 is inhaled pirfenidone, the same molecule as generic oral drug, and PureTech's Ph3 is already dosing. A $1.3B cap with $387M cash is rich ahead of the MIST Ph2b FVC readout in 2H 2027.
AARD: Full cardiac clinical hold and a terminated HERO Ph3 leave no live program, and VYKAT already owns PWS label; a value trap until a path emerges, despite cash at 3.1x $29M cap.
ARWR: Plozasiran is approved for FCS and the sHTG sNDA is under priority review, backed by SHASTA-3/4 (TG -79%/-81%). Ionis leads in sHTG by 6-12 months, and the $6.2B cap already reflects a lot.
DNLI: Avlayah Q3 revenue of $17.8M beat the $10-12M guide and Q4 is guided to $30-32M. The LRRK2 Ph2b failure in idiopathic PD limits the pipeline story; $3.4B cap vs $1.0B cash.
AMLX: Positive Ph3 in post-bariatric hypoglycemia (55% fewer Level 2/3 events, p=0.000003) with no approved rival and an NDA next. After a 93% 12-month run, the $3.6B cap prices in much of that success.
GLUE: GFORCE-1 (n=108) cut NEK7 80-90% and hsCRP 85% with no SAEs, and $578M cash is 62% of the $933M cap. Efficacy is unproven: gout Ph2 data is 2H27 and Novo's ziltivekimab leads in CV inflammation by ~2 years.
EXOZ: Successful 100-liter pilot run is manufacturing progress, not drug development; w a preclinical compound, $6M cash (1.2 quarters) and a $38M cap, dilution is near-certain event.
BIOA: QUELL-CV Ph2 reads 12-week hsCRP in Q4 2026 after ~86% Ph1 reductions. Cash of $352M exceeds the $240M cap, but MACE benefit is unproven and Novo's injectable ziltivekimab is further along.
VCEL: Q3 revenue rose 26% to $85.4M (MACI +21%, burn care +52%) and FY26 guidance rose to $344-346M, yet a $2.9B cap is ~8.5x that revenue. Up 53% in 12 months, it leaves little room before the Q1 2027 guide.
TRDA: Cash of $193M covers 91% of the $213M cap, cushioning the downside, but Cohort 1 (n=8) moved dystrophin only +2.36% over a 4.00% baseline. Cohort 1 data are due by YE2026 and the 12 mg/kg cohort in Q1 2027.
SRRK: ISEMBYLD was approved Sep 11 and the SMA launch is underway, with EU opinion expected 1H 2027. But a $5.9B cap on ~$1M quarterly revenue prices in a lot for an add-on to near-normalizing therapies; obesity is unproven.
OVID: A $519M cap for a drug with no efficacy data yet; the more-potent vigabatrin successor has only Ph1 target-engagement data. $161M cash runs into 2029, so the Q1 2027 photosensitivity study and 2H 2027 focal Ph2 are the tests.
PRTA: Cash of $271M is 66% of the $409M cap. Prasinezumab's Ph2b narrowly missed (HR 0.84, p=0.0657), Ph3 PARAISO completes in 2029, and Prothena gets only royalties and milestones.
AXSM: Auvelity won approval for Alzheimer's agitation on Apr 30, and quarterly revenue is $260M against a $7.2B cap. Solriamfetol Ph3 (1Q27) and the AXS-12 PDUFA (May 1, 2027) add further catalysts.
PMN: PRECISE-AD is fully enrolled (144) w zero ARIA-E at 6-month blinded look, while unblinded efficacy has slipped to early 2027; cash of $64M is 2x $32M cap.
QURE: BLA accepted with a May 1, 2027 PDUFA, based on 12 patients versus an external control (75% cUHDRS slowing at 3 years) and after FDA reversals. Cash of $768M covers $548M of debt.
ACAD: Q3 revenue rose 23% to $342M, with FY26 guidance of $1.265-1.295B, so the $3.2B cap is about 2.5x sales, backed by $976M cash. Remlifanserin missed its Ph2 primary (p=0.0603), so that bet is unproven.
ANIK: FDA found the Hyalofast PMA not approvable (Oct 2026) and Cingal is ex-US only, with a US NDA not planned until end-2027. Still, a $170M cap sits against $45M cash and ~$31M quarterly revenue.
COLL: Q3 product revenue grew 3% to $216.3M as JORNAY PM rose 24% while the pain portfolio fell 18%. FY26 guidance of $825-855M was reaffirmed; $1.08B debt against $145M cash makes paydown the lever.
GHRS: Inhaled GH001 posted MADRS -15.5 vs placebo at Day 8 in a Ph2b TRD trial, and the FDA hold lifted Jan 2026. With $351M cash against a $1.3B cap, the Q1 2027 end-of-Ph2 meeting is the next gate.
LPCN: PPD Ph3 missed its ITT primary and rescue is a post hoc subgroup (n=54) w litigation overhang, so $23M cash at 1.8x $13M cap is cheap for a reason.
EBS: NARCAN is eroding: Q3 revenue fell 52% to $110M, naloxone fell 42% to $43.5M and FY26 guidance was cut to $600-645M. Debt of $514M exceeds the $299M cap; $176M cash cushions but does not fix it.
ATTO: Single-dose Ph1b showed CPUO PP-NRS4 of 82% vs 22% placebo and about 95% IL-31 suppression, with cash at 59% of a $673M cap. AD cohort is small (18 vs 8), Ph2 starts 1H 2027, and Nemluvio and Dupixent set the bar.
MSLE: Open-label grip gains and a fat-fraction dip from 49.7% to 46.0% in 4 adults are the hook; placebo-controlled BASECAMP reads Q1 2027. $53M cash is a third of the $159M cap, so funding is needed; stock is up ~12x in a year.
BNTX: Cash of $18.6B covers most of the $21B cap, so little is paid for pumitamig, whose Ph3 trials have no randomized data yet. Ivonescimab leads the PD-1xVEGF class, and 2026 revenue guidance was cut.
IAM: IAM1363 shows 36% systemic PR (19/53) and 41% intracranial PR (9/22), but zongertinib, T-DXd and tucatinib crowd the HER2 field. Cash is 74% of the $280M cap; shares traded below the $16 IPO price.
XFOR: WHIM revenue is $2.9M a quarter, so the $362M cap (cash $188M, debt $77M) rides on the 4WARD Ph3 in neutropenia (n=126, topline Q1 2028). Cheap generic G-CSF sets a high bar.
ALLO: Cema-cel cleared MRD in 7 of 12 patients vs 2 of 12 on observation, with RMAT and Fast Track. The ALPHA3 interim EFS in mid-2027 is a binary test; cash of $389M funds it and exceeds the $281M cap.
IPHA: Lacutamab showed 43% ORR in Sezary syndrome with ~26-month mDOR, but Poteligeo is the approved standard. Sobi partnership extends runway to Q1 2028; cash of $130M covers most of the $142M cap.
DMRA: A $1.8B cap rests on preclinical data only; first-in-human CLARITY-101 proof-of-concept is not due until mid-2027. Cash is $529M, so the valuation is far ahead of any human evidence.
RIGL: Commercial revenue of about $290M a year (Tavalisse, Rezlidhia and the Aug-launched Veppanu) puts the $823M cap near 2.8x sales, a fair price for the base business, so the premium rests on R289. Its 33-40% transfusion independence in a small Ph1b has to beat approved imetelstat and luspatercept (~38-40%); ASH in Dec is the test.
AAPG: Olverembatinib shows 61% MMR at 2 years in 2L CML and its China NRDL listing was renewed, but US differentiation vs asciminib is unproven. At a $1.2B cap, cash of $280M sits below $309M of debt, so the upside needs the global Ph3s (lisaftoclax ~Oct 2027).
BCYC: A $223M cap vs $470M cash prices zelenectide as nearly dead. Duravelo-2 (randomized Ph2, EV+pembro bar of ~31 mo mOS) reads 2H 2027, with the nuzefatide PDAC Ph2 as a free option.
NBP: Ph1b ORR of 75-77% and 82% 6-mo PFS in 1L CLDN18.2 gastric, with an FDA-confirmed ORR-based accelerated path and Ph3 start targeted Q4 2026. Cash of $191M vs $211M cap, but the data are single-arm and the field is crowded.
RNXT: Interim mOS 16 vs 10mo (p=0.051) leans positive w enrollment done and topline 2H27, so short carries squeeze risk; cap is $53M.
RVMD: Daraxonrasib doubled 2L PDAC survival (OS HR 0.40) and is approved, w $39.9B cap; 1L data and launch uptake are swing.
AKTS: Ph1b AKY-1189 (Ac-225 Nectin-4) has no efficacy data yet and enters against approved enfortumab vedotin (Padcev, since 2019). The $899M cap rests on preliminary data due Q1 2027; $493M cash runs into 2029.
TLX: Q3 revenue of $245M (+19%) is real, but a $3.0B cap sits against $252M cash and $600M debt, and the $1.65B ITM acquisition adds $302M of assumed ITM net debt (Telix holders keep about 76% of the combined group; shareholder vote Dec 1) plus ITM-11 CRL risk (Aug 7). Pluvicto is years ahead and ProstACT Part 2 has no disclosed readout date.
CELC: REVTORPYK cut progression/death 76% (HR ~0.24) and launched Sep 30 with no direct wild-type rival. Cash is $643M against $754M debt; the PIK3CA-mutant sNDA is the next lever for a $3.3B cap.
OKUR: Reset to preclinical after deprioritizing OKI-219; OKI-345 IND is H1 2027, 1+ year behind Ph3 zovegalisib and approved PI3K rivals. Cash of $163M exceeds the $137M cap, but that is not enough.
VSTM: The KRAS G12D inhibitor, not the ovarian launch, is the thesis, and early pancreatic response rates are encouraging. But Revolution Medicines and others are racing in the same space and the price already credits a good outcome.
ANIX: No confirmed RECIST responses after 14 CAR-T patients over four years, and the TNBC vaccine Ph2 has no date. With $14M cash against an $89M cap, dilution looks near-certain.
CHRS: The $82M cap roughly matches $84M cash, with $53M debt and only 2.5 quarters of runway. Loqtorzi earned $14.0M in Q3; casdozokitug HCC data in 1H27 are the swing factor.
NUVB: Ibtrozi is the most prescribed ROS1 TKI in new starts, with Q3 sales of $27.5M (+18% QoQ) and 49.7-mo median DOR. Still, the $1.4B cap is large next to $663M cash and $454M debt.
STRO: STRO-004 shows partial responses across three tumor types (n=49) but discloses no ORR or PFS, and Tivdak is already approved. $249M debt offsets $142M cash against a $155M cap; data due 1H 2027.
LTRN: $6M cap against $6M cash buys an FDA-aligned single-arm L858R study (8.3mo mPFS vs 3-5mo for chemo), but ~2 quarters of runway makes dilution near-certain; option value only.
IMMP: After NSCLC Ph3 stopped for futility and market doubts manufacturing fix, STS data (51.5% vs ~15%) is show-me; $99M cash is 3.8x $26M cap, w 2.2 quarters of runway.
SLGL: Patidegib's Ph3 topline lands in late Nov 2026, with a 9% dropout rate and US rights retained behind it. A $180M cap against $46M cash makes this a binary readout on a niche indication.
AURA: CoMpass Ph3 is fully enrolled (108 patients) under an SPA with topline 2H 2027, and bel-sar has no approved vision-sparing 1L rival. An $802M cap vs $297M cash leaves limited room before the binary.
PLRX: 1 CR and 2 PRs in n=16 ICI-refractory patients (vs ~10% historical) earn nothing, w cash 3.4x $50M cap; Mar-2027 Ph1b interim is re-rate in a crowded space.
CYTK: Approved, expanding label, and ahead of Edgewise in time and evidence. But the price already assumes a leading HCM franchise, and debt-like liabilities and a modest effect size cap the enthusiasm.
LGVN: ELPIS II missed its primary RVEF endpoint (p=0.8336); the MACE signal (1 vs 8 events) is secondary. The FDA meeting is unscheduled, a strategic review is open, and $7.2M cash lasts into Q1 2027, so dilution looks likely.
IKT: No efficacy data yet for this imatinib prodrug in PAH; the Part A interim (n=50) in 1H27 is safety only. $193M cash funds through Part B topline, but any add-on must beat sotatercept and avoid the tolerability that hurt Gleevec.
ABSI: A $1.3B cap on Phase 1 safety and a ~65-day half-life only, with no efficacy data yet. The Dec 2026 13-week AGA interim faces finasteride and MANE's more advanced VDPHL01.
FBIO: A $205M PRV sale (closed Mar 2026) and $152M cash sit against a $57M cap, pricing ZYCUBO and Journey derm near zero. Holding-company complexity and 3.8 quarters of runway explain the discount.
LCTX: OpRegen showed +6.2 ETDRS letters and RPE re-appearance at 36 months, but in 5 uncontrolled patients. The Genentech-run Ph2a has no guided data date, so this needs patience; Syfovre and Izervay lead GA.
KOD: Ph3 wins in wet AMD (p=0.0007, 54% at 6-month dosing) support a Q4 BLA, but only show non-inferiority to aflibercept. With $89M cash against a $6.3B cap and KSI-101 PEAK due in Dec, dilution risk is real.
SGP: BIM-IOL's first-in-human data show 37% mean IOP reduction and 86% off drops at 4 years, but it is a small study and Ph3s finish enrolling only in 2027. $216M cash funds into 2028; iDose TR and Durysta are approved.
ARDX: IBSRELA grew 23% to $96.3M in Q3, but FY26 guidance was cut to $350-370M on payer friction. The $823M cap is about 1.6x annualized revenue; ACCEL Ph3 in CIC reads out 2H27.
NSRX: Faster PK than EpiPen (T100 1.69 vs 3.47 min) is real, but w $0 cash and a pivotal still to fund, dilution comes first at $35M cap.
EVMN: EVO756 missed all endpoints in AD (n=121) and CSU, leaving EVO301 (Ph2a n=70, EASI -55% vs -22%) with a Ph2b only in mid-2027. $262M cash supports a $304M cap, about 10 quarters of runway, in a crowded AD field.
ABVX: Obefazimod posted 39.3% placebo-adjusted maintenance remission in UC, ahead of the oral peers listed, and an NDA is due by end-2026. At a $6.7B cap with $459M cash, the open question is launch share, not efficacy.
MNKD: Q3 revenue rose 24% to $101.9M (Afrezza $19.3M, Furoscix $22.4M), but $567M debt against $97M cash and a $1.3B cap leaning on royalties leave little room until Afrezza pediatric uptake shows.
MAZE: MZE829 cut uACR 35.6% on average (FSGS 61.8% vs ~43% for Vertex's inaxaplin) in open-label n=12-15 data. A $2.0B cap already prices in a lot; final data early 2027 and a pivotal start follow.
ACET: 7-patient allogeneic CAR-T lupus signal stays intact and is cash-backed ($138M, ~5x $28M cap); slipped data timing and durability are risks.
ATYR: Ph3 EFZO-FIT missed (p=0.33); the new FVC-primary Ph3 rests on a 44-patient post-hoc subgroup and depends on finding a licensee. $514M cap vs $50M cash after a ~530% 12-month run.
IMUX: Both relapsing-MS Ph3s (1,121 and 1,100 pts) are fully enrolled with futility passed; topline Dec 2026, NDA mid-2027 if positive. $307M cap vs $132M cash (4.4 quarters), against ocrelizumab and ofatumumab.
CRDL: Pivotal MAVERIC withdrawal-design Ph3 reads Aug 2027-Feb 2028, and ARCALYST is the entrenched IL-1 standard. With $29M cash and about 5.6 quarters of runway, funding is the issue.
PHAR: A real approved product growing nicely in an ultra-rare disease, but a guidance cut and leadership change are fresh. Fairly priced; the pediatric label is the next test.
NKTR: REZPEG hit its 393-patient AD Ph2b (p<0.001, Lancet) and cash is $953M against a $1.3B cap. The wait is long: first Ph3 AD topline is mid-2028, against entrenched dupilumab.
IFRX: Izicopan has only Ph1 safety/PK/PD and a 4-week HS/CSU Ph2a signal, with the renal AAV Ph2 starting early 2027. The $174M cap sits below $179M cash, so the market ascribes little value to the pipeline.
CUE: Randomized CSU Ph2 (n=145) beat placebo (54/53/43% responders vs 11%), but $58M cash is only 3.4 quarters. A raise looks likely before the global Ph2b/3 starts; the $149M cap is up 1,900% in a year.
ARTV: AlloNK was discontinued Oct 27 and Ph3 will not start; a strategic review (merger, sale or liquidation) has no timing. Cash of $319M exceeds the $202M cap, so the outcome and burn drive value.
MCRB: 77% cut in bloodstream infections in allo-HSCT (Breakthrough) at $14M cap, below $18M cash, but ~1.5 quarters of runway and an unfunded pivotal Ph2 make it a financing-gated option.
ABUS: Moderna has paid $950M (Arbutus share $178.4M) and up to $1.3B more hinges on a 28 USC 1498 ruling, argued Nov 5 with no date. Imdusiran's 8 functional cures sit in a crowded HBV field.
ENTA: Zelicapavir cut hospitalization to 1.7% vs 5.0% and symptoms 6.7 days faster in a high-risk Ph2b subset, which still needs confirming. Cap less cash is ~$116M as RESOLVE starts and LOTUS reads 1Q 2027.
INO: VOCERYQ won accelerated approval in RRP (81% fewer surgeries at 52 wk, n=32), with shipping due about late Dec. Cash of $48M against a $336M cap and 2.6 quarters of runway make funding the issue.
BHC: With $20.2B of debt (6.3x the $3.2B cap), Xifaxan generics expected in 2028 and RED-C failed, larsucosterol is a minor option. Its Ph2b missed the survival primary and Ph3 is still in planning.
INKT: Randomized ARDS Ph2 reads out in 2H26 and a win would dwarf $51M cap, but $10M cash (3.5 quarters) means any pop is likely funded by dilution; binary w a financing tail.
CTNM: $245M cash funds the company to mid-2029, which cushions the downside. Still, PROPEL-IPF has no guided topline, PIPE-791 trails BMS's admilparant, and the pain crossover showed no clear significance.
ENTX: EB613 has Ph2 data (n=161) and an FDA-supported single Ph3 (~750 women, hip BMD at 12 months). $266M cash funds it into 2030, so the $599M cap rests on execution, not financing.
EDIT: EDIT-401 has only primate data (~90% LDL-C cut) and no human data yet; first dosing is due by YE2026 and safety data in Q1 2027. Verve is 2-3 years ahead in humans, and $190M cash is under 8 quarters.
RARE: Crysvita ($109M of $173M Q3 revenue) anchors a $730-760M FY26 guide; GENGLYCOS and FAYUVI are approved and GTX-102 missed its Ph3 endpoints. $1.6B cap vs $401M cash and $1.2B debt.
RZLT: upLIFT topline lands mid-Dec 2026 on a single-arm, open-label n=16 study (7 of 8 early patients responded), after the congenital-HI Ph3 missed. $90M cash is about 5 quarters, so a miss leaves little cushion.
AMRN: A $238M cap sits below $323M of cash, with three straight quarters of positive cash flow and a completed $70M+ cost program. US sales are flat near $36M a quarter and a strategic review is pending.
RYTM: Imcivree sells about $92M a quarter, but EMANATE failed all four cohorts and the story now leans on bivamelagon in acquired hypothalamic obesity, with Ph3 start due by YE2026. A $7.7B cap leaves little margin.
VANI: SLIM-1 (n=10 per arm, 4 wks): weight loss 0.79% vs 0.82% on Wegovy, 0/10 vs 5/10 AEs, not built for efficacy. Financing is the near-term issue at $15M cash vs a $95M cap; Novo evaluation ongoing.
EWTX: A cleaner safety profile would be a real differentiator, but 53 open-label patients over 12 weeks do not prove it. Cytokinetics is approved and has randomized data; Edgewise has to earn the premium.
CAPR: A Nov 22 FDA decision follows a 3-9 adcom vote against, so the outcome is binary on a narrowed upper-limb label (HOPE-3 n=106, p=0.03). $199M cash is 41% of the $483M cap; an activist is pushing the board.
MENS: The US pivotal failed vs placebo and the original source is unavailable, so a comparability study delays a combined NDA to 2029-2030. $1M cash against a $135M cap points to near-term dilution.
STOK: Zorevunersen showed about 80% durable seizure reduction plus cognitive gains, with no approved disease-modifier in SCN1A Dravet. But EMPEROR Ph3 reads out only in Q3 2027 and cash is $359M.
DSGN: The $635M cap is 3.0x its $209M cash, resting on 4-week data (frataxin mRNA +65% in blood). 12-week durability is due Q1 2027, and Larimar's frataxin BLA is already submitted.
AVXL: EMA MAA was withdrawn Mar 25 after a negative CHMP, and a new US Ph3 has no start date. Cash of $118M (1.6x the $76M cap) is thin comfort after an 86% fall in 12 months.
COYA: No efficacy data until the ALSTARS 24-week topline in early Q2 2027. Cash of $36M is about half the $70M cap and funds only into 2H 2027, while AMX0035 and tofersen are already approved.
ATHE: FDA aligned on one ~200-patient pivotal Ph3 at 50 mg after a 48% UMSARS-I slowing in Ph2, but the trial is unfunded and 75 mg was not significant. With $27M cash against a $431M cap, partnering or a raise likely comes first.
IGC: Almost no cash (about 0.1 quarter of runway) ahead of CALMA topline; interim CMAI -10.45 at p=0.071 is borderline, so dilution risk outweighs $19M cap.
TNXP: Tonmya is ramping (Q2 $11.0M, +197% QoQ), yet 3.8 quarters of runway at ~$40M quarterly burn means financing, not demand, sets path; cash of $163M is 3.1x $52M cap.
CING: CTx-1301 met its Ph3 endpoints, and the June CRL was over manufacturing only. Resubmission is due Dec 2026-Jan 2027, but 3.4 quarters of runway and a crowded stimulant field make financing the question.
SPTX: Well funded, with $404M cash and runway into 2029, but a $1.0B cap credits GlyphAllo before any Ph2b efficacy data. BUOY-1 (up to 360 patients) reads 1H 2027, against approved zuranolone.
LBRX: NOVA-2 enrollment ran ahead of plan, pulling Ph3 topline into 1H 2027. A $1.5B cap with $404M cash must be earned against cheap D2 generics and newly approved Cobenfy; LB-102 needs a tolerability edge.
ACHV: Cytisinicline's June CRL was for CMC and labeling only, and ORCA-2 abstinence was 32.6% vs 7.0% placebo. Resubmission is on track for Q4 2026; $202M cash against a $667M cap.
BLSM: SOLARA's 45% ORR (18/40) and 88% DCR in C797S+ NSCLC are encouraging but single-arm with 6.9-mo follow-up. A $434M cap against $225M cash; pivotal SOLARA-2 starts Q1 2027.
YARW: YB-101 (anti-TSHR, Fast Track) is dosing but has no efficacy data until 2H 2027. $269M cash gives runway into 2030, so this is a wait for Ph2a proof of concept at a $490M cap.
ADRX: Cash is $901M against a $1.5B cap, but human efficacy in HAE patients is n=3 open-label. Ph3 STOP-HAE reads out by YE2027 against established Takeda and Ionis drugs plus CRISPR and long-acting rivals.
LYCA: A $1.6B cap after an October IPO rests on a 96% free-IgE cut in a small healthy-atopic cohort. Xolair already depletes IgE, Celldex is ahead in CSU, and the lock-up expiry looms; cash is $429M.
KROS: Cash of $260M exceeds the $199M cap, but cibotercept failed in PAH and rinvatercept has only Ph1 healthy-volunteer data in DMD. Ph2 dosing began Sep 28 with data in 1H 2027; prior myostatin drugs disappointed.
ADCT: The stock fell 57% on LOTIS-5 after a PFS win (HR 0.73) came with more deaths, and FDA raised benefit-risk questions. Zynlonta sells ~$21M a quarter; $271M cap vs $189M cash and $420M debt.
CTOR: Lymphir shipments rose 120% q/q to 792 units, with 54 ordering institutions, but it faces entrenched Poteligeo in CTCL. A $57M cap with $17M cash points to near-term financing; 10-K due Dec.
SLBT: No clinical data: FDA found its CD19 Armed-T packages insufficient and the glioblastoma IND is not targeted until Q3 2027. A $404M cap is 50x its $8M cash, against $1.39M of H1 revenue.
PRLD: PRT12396 sits under an Incyte option expiring Feb 2027, and PRT13722 only just entered Phase 1 with no human efficacy data. Cash is 45% of the $335M cap after a 109% 12-month run-up.
KPTI: SENTRY hit SVR35 (49.8% vs 28%) but missed TSS co-primary w Grade 3+ AEs 70% vs 50%; w $91M cash dwarfing a ~$1M micro-cap, SVR-only sNDA is a cheap binary on FDA.
ADAG: Cash of $128M nearly matches the $134M cap, while muzastotug posted 31% ORR at 20mg/kg (n=26) in MSS CRC, though 10mg/kg fell to 13%. Agenus's exit helps; a randomized Ph2 reads 1H 2027.
AGEN: NEST showed 32% pCR with no recurrences at median 32.2 mo, but ROBBIN Ph3 has not started (first patient Q1 2027). With $87M cash vs $239M debt and $85M upfront funding only into Q3 2027, dilution is the swing factor.
LNTH: Price tracks Curium's $102.50 cash plus up to $12 CVR offer (close 1H 2027), with FTC HSR review extended Oct 21. Pylarify sales were flat at $238.9M (-0.7%); deal completion is the issue.
TVRD: H2 HCC topline is binary: only biomarker/PK data, a hard STAT3 history and a going-concern flag mean a stock trading at about its $16M cash is no floor.
